rationales.A: The engraving is dated to the Haymarket bombing: a speaker on a wagon, police in smoke, and the Jefferson Street sign.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Homestead was a steel strike in Pennsylvania in 1892, not a bombing at a Chicago rally.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Pullman was a railroad strike in Chicago in 1894, not a bombing at a rally.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the 1877 strike was a railroad walkout, not a bombing at a rally.
rationales.general:
Name what is drawn before naming the event.
1. A speaker stands on a wagon, addressing a crowd.
2. Police move through thick smoke as men fall in the street.
3. The street sign reads N. Jefferson St., in Chicago.
4. A bomb blast at a Chicago labor rally is the Haymarket affair of 1886.
Remember: place, crowd, and blast together name the event.

stimulus.text: Harper’s Weekly engraving of the Haymarket Square bombing in Chicago, May 4, 1886. At the left, a speaker stands on a wagon with one arm raised, addressing the crowd. In the center, police officers move through thick smoke as the bomb explodes, and men fall and scatter in the street. A street sign on a building at the upper left reads “N. JEFFERSON ST.”
